question: Why is careful monitoring of IV fluids especially vital during labor for a mother with kidney disease?

options.A: Excess fluids stop the uterus from contracting normally after the baby is born
options.B: Compromised kidneys cannot handle fluid overload, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema
options.C: Too much intravenous fluid causes the infant's kidneys to stop working permanently
options.D: Intravenous fluids react badly with standard pain medications used in labor

explanation: Weakened kidneys can't get rid of extra water well, so giving too much IV fluid can cause it to back right up into her lungs.

question: Which environmental issue is a major breeding ground for malaria mosquitoes in local neighborhoods?

options.A: Thick concrete flooring inside residential buildings
options.B: Blocked drainage channels and stagnant water pools
options.C: Dry sandy soil found in northern farming regions
options.D: Solar panels installed on health center roofs

explanation: Mosquitoes love standing water! Blocked drains and puddles give them a safe place to lay eggs, which drives up malaria rates.

question: What is a common myth that scares many Nigerian women away from using modern birth control?

options.A: Fear of permanent infertility or severe side effects
options.B: Idea that injections cause immediate hair loss
options.C: Belief that birth control methods are free of charge
options.D: Assumption that pills increase visual acuity

explanation: Correct! Worries about permanent barrenness or scary side effects are major barriers we encounter in community practice.

question: Why is primary health care considered the bedrock of a solid health system?

options.A: It focuses solely on emergency trauma surgeries
options.B: It is funded entirely by international donors rather than local governments
options.C: It eliminates the need for any specialized doctors or hospitals
options.D: It prevents minor health issues from becoming major hospital burdens by catching them early

explanation: By offering promotive and preventive services early at the community level, PHC stops health problems from escalating. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why was the Basel Convention created back in the late 1980s?

options.A: Global hospitals were running out of space for medical syringes
options.B: Oceans were overflowing with plastic beverage containers
options.C: Air pollution from factories caused a sudden rise in global temperatures
options.D: Industrialized nations were dumping toxic waste in developing countries

explanation: Spot on! Wealthy countries used to ship their toxic industrial byproducts to poorer nations to save money. Public outrage over this unfair practice led directly to the treaty.

question: Which of these is a major headache for tracking nursing costs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive use of automated digital billing
options.B: Reliance on manual record-keeping systems
options.C: Universal health insurance coverage for all citizens
options.D: Complete elimination of out-of-pocket purchases

explanation: When everything is on paper, it becomes very difficult to quickly track exact nursing hours and supplies used.

question: What is the big advantage of using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) right at the bedside?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for blood tests and lab work
options.B: It removes all risk of infection during invasive procedures
options.C: It gives immediate answers at the bedside without moving the patient
options.D: It produces permanent color photographs without using sound waves

explanation: POCUS lets you peek inside and check organs instantly without having to transport a fragile patient out of the unit.

question: Why must disposable medical supplies never be reused for another patient?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination between patients
options.B: Because manufacturers forbid manual cleaning
options.C: Because the plastic degrades if washed once
options.D: To make more room in hospital supply rooms

explanation: Single-use items are made for one time only. Tossing them out after use stops infections from spreading between patients.

question: How can a nurse best reassure a patient who has mild pregnancy nausea?

options.A: You must take prescription drugs immediately to protect the fetus.
options.B: Mild nausea and vomiting typically do not harm the developing baby.
options.C: Eating large meals will cure the queasiness within hours.
options.D: The symptoms will disappear completely by the second week.

explanation: Mums worry the baby isn't eating enough. Letting them know that mild early nausea won't hurt their little one brings great peace of mind!

question: Why do you pull the skin taut instead of pinching it before an intradermal injection?

options.A: Taut skin makes the needle sharper as it enters
options.B: Pinching causes severe bruising around the injection site
options.C: Pinching the skin lifts it and accidentally creates a subcutaneous pocket
options.D: Pulling the skin taut numbs the nerve endings temporarily

explanation: Well done! Pinching bunches up the fatty layer underneath, making it way too easy to accidentally slide past the dermis.

question: You see a flash of blood, but when you try to slide the plastic cannula forward, it feels stuck and the patient winces in pain. What likely happened?

options.A: The IV fluid is running at an incorrect rate
options.B: The skin antiseptic was not allowed to dry
options.C: The needle punctured through the back wall of the vein
options.D: The tourniquet was removed too early

explanation: Ah, you might have gone right through the back wall! It happens to everyone when learning. Take a breath, pull back safely, and try a fresh spot.

question: How does a nurse properly assess a patient's resting muscle tone?

options.A: By asking the patient to push hard against the nurse's hand
options.B: By observing the patient walk across the hospital room
options.C: By measuring the circumference of the limb with a tape
options.D: By feeling the resistance of the muscle during a passive stretch

explanation: Muscle tone is the resting tension of a muscle. You check this by gently moving the patient's limb for them and feeling how the muscle resists.

question: What happens to a DRF if hospital staff constantly collect drugs on credit and fail to pay back?

options.A: The suppliers will double the credit period for future orders
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically start generating higher profits
options.C: The fund will quickly experience cash depletion and stockouts
options.D: The government will automatically inject fresh emergency funds

explanation: Unpaid credit creates holes in the system. If the cash doesn't come back in, the pharmacy won't have money to buy new medicines when patients need them.

question: What is the direct result of a lipid-soluble hormone binding to its intracellular receptor?

options.A: Sudden release of stored calcium from vesicles
options.B: Immediate breakdown of cell membrane channels
options.C: Changes in gene expression and protein synthesis
options.D: Immediate activation of cyclic AMP molecules

explanation: The hormone-receptor complex interacts directly with DNA to turn genes on or off, creating new functional proteins. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h4)

question: You feel the uterus and it is soft and boggy right after delivery. What is your very first action?

options.A: Apply warm compresses to the lower back
options.B: Administer oral pain relief medication
options.C: Transfer the patient to a tertiary hospital immediately
options.D: Perform immediate fundal uterine massage

explanation: Massage helps the uterine muscles tighten up and clamp down on bleeding vessels. It's a quick, lifesaving first step!

question: A school nurse notices several students rubbing their eyes and squinting at the chalkboard. What should she do?

options.A: Vision screening assessments
options.B: Playground safety audits
options.C: Emergency vaccination drives
options.D: Nutritional cooking classes

explanation: You nailed it! Squinting at the board is a classic sign of eye trouble, so a quick vision check is the best next step.

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Acute bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Hypertension is directly linked to sodium intake, making salt restriction a primary medical intervention for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: What does the acronym HEADSS stand for in adolescent nursing assessments?

options.A: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide
options.B: Heart, Ears, Abdomen, Drugs, Skin, Skeleton
options.C: Health, Exercise, Anatomy, Diet, Sleep, Symptoms
options.D: Hospital, Environment, Age, Diagnosis, Surgery, Status

explanation: HEADSS is a psychosocial screening tool used to evaluate key areas of an adolescent's life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient says her periods always arrive every 28 days, last 5 days, and have a moderate flow. What is your best initial nursing action?

options.A: Document this as a normal finding in her chart
options.B: Instruct her to start taking oral contraceptives
options.C: Order emergency hormone blood tests
options.D: Refer her immediately to a gynecological surgeon

explanation: A classic 28-day cycle with moderate flow is textbook normal! No interventions or emergency tests are needed—just a clean, accurate chart entry.

question: Where should used injection needles be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: A red biohazard bag for soft waste
options.B: A standard black plastic trash bag
options.C: A rigid, puncture-proof sharps container
options.D: The side pocket of the nurse's uniform

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries for nurses and housekeeping staff. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: What happens to the heart muscle fibers during Ventricular Fibrillation?

options.A: They beat together in a slow, steady rhythm
options.B: They rest without any electrical signals at all
options.C: They become completely stiff and cannot relax
options.D: They twitch randomly without pumping any blood

explanation: During VF, the heart muscle fibers flutter and twitch chaotically like a bag of worms. Because they aren't working together, no blood is pumped to the body.

question: Why are the three semicircular canals placed at right angles to each other?

options.A: To make room for the auditory nerve inside the skull
options.B: To detect rotational movement in all three spatial dimensions
options.C: To allow equal pressure distribution of perilymph fluid
options.D: To prevent the endolymph from flowing too quickly

explanation: This clever layout lets your brain pick up movement in every direction: up and down, side to side, and tilting! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which IV fluid is the ONLY one safe to use alongside blood products?

options.A: Ringer's Lactate Solution
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: Half-Normal Saline

explanation: Normal saline is isotonic and friendly to red blood cells, preventing them from bursting or clumping like other fluids might.

question: A patient asks you about the structure of the clitoris. What is a key fact to share with her?

options.A: It disappears completely after a woman goes through puberty.
options.B: It functions mainly to produce mucus for vaginal lubrication.
options.C: It is an internal gland located right next to the cervix.
options.D: Only a small part of it is visible externally, while most extends deep inside.

explanation: You're learning fast! Only the tip (glans) is seen on the outside; the rest of the structure extends deep inside the pelvis.

question: Which of these is a very common mental health challenge for survivors of ongoing abuse?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Well done! Survivors often deal with lasting emotional impacts like anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

question: When should you, as the nurse, do your final dosage calculation?

options.A: Only when the pharmacist calls
options.B: Right before giving the drug
options.C: After a bad reaction happens
options.D: During your annual nursing review

explanation: Always double-check your math right before administration. It is your last chance to catch mistakes before the drug enters the patient's body.

question: What is the big benefit of using a head-to-toe approach for a physical exam?

options.A: It requires the patient to change positions constantly
options.B: It allows the nurse to finish the examination in under two minutes
options.C: It eliminates the need to inspect the skin
options.D: It ensures a structured and thorough assessment without missing body parts

explanation: Going head-to-toe builds a solid routine. It makes sure you never accidentally skip checking an important body system!

question: Which of these details is NOT needed in your nursing notes after an ear irrigation?

options.A: How the ear canal looked afterward
options.B: The amount and temperature of the fluid used
options.C: The brand name of the plastic syringe used
options.D: How well the patient tolerated the procedure

explanation: You need to document clinical facts like fluid amounts and patient reactions, but nobody needs to know the syringe brand name!

question: Which of these is NOT a main focus of community-level diabetes education?

options.A: Dispelling cultural myths about the causes of chronic illness
options.B: Teaching healthy food substitutions using local ingredients
options.C: Promoting expensive surgical weight-loss procedures for all citizens
options.D: Encouraging affordable physical activity like brisk walking

explanation: Community education focuses on practical, low-cost steps like eating local healthy foods and walking. Expensive surgeries are definitely not standard community advice!

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a quarantined person develops a sudden fever?

options.A: Reclassify the person as a suspected case and arrange for testing
options.B: Discharge the person immediately to clear space in the facility
options.C: Administer strong antibiotics without informing the doctor
options.D: Tell the person to ignore it until the quarantine period ends

explanation: Developing symptoms means the person may now be infected and requires prompt isolation and diagnostic evaluation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT linked to problems in the limbic system?

options.A: Major depressive disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Correct! Iron deficiency anemia is a blood and nutrition issue, whereas anxiety, depression, and PTSD are all tied to limbic system imbalances.

question: Why does a reentry circuit cause an arrhythmia?

options.A: It forces the heart muscle cells to permanently stop receiving oxygen
options.B: It traps an electrical signal in a looping pathway that causes rapid contractions
options.C: It immediately destroys the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.D: It completely blocks all electrical impulses from leaving the sinoatrial node

explanation: A reentry circuit occurs when an electrical wave gets stuck traveling in a circle, constantly re-stimulating the heart tissue to beat too fast. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: A client wants a refill for her birth control, but admits she might already be pregnant. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform a pregnancy test before giving the refill
options.B: Tell her to double her dose for the next week
options.C: Switch her to a progestin-only pill right away
options.D: Refill the prescription immediately without questions

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out an existing pregnancy before continuing hormonal contraceptives to protect both the client and potential pregnancy.

question: Which protective gear is a must-have when working near an active X-ray machine?

options.A: Thick rubber industrial gloves
options.B: Lead apron and thyroid collar
options.C: N95 respiratory face mask
options.D: Waterproof plastic shoe covers

explanation: Lead aprons and thyroid shields act like a block, stopping harmful radiation from reaching your sensitive organs and tissues.

question: Why should a nurse NOT apply a warm poultice to a fresh injury that happened ten minutes ago?

options.A: It turns the skin completely white permanently
options.B: It freezes the tissue and causes gangrene
options.C: It cures the injury too fast for proper charting
options.D: It increases local blood flow and worsens bleeding

explanation: Heat causes blood vessels to open up, which increases bleeding and swelling immediately after a fresh trauma. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of intra-natal care?

options.A: Achieving a safe delivery for mother and baby
options.B: Ensuring the mother sleeps through delivery
options.C: Speeding up the duration of the first stage
options.D: Preventing the need for any pain relief

explanation: The main focus of intra-natal care is to safeguard the health and well-being of both the mother and the newborn throughout labor and birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: What is a main duty of Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) in a PHC clinic?

options.A: Performing major specialized surgical operations independently
options.B: Managing hospital-wide administrative budgets and procurement
options.C: Handling international health policy formulation and funding
options.D: Diagnosing and treating minor ailments using standing orders

explanation: CHEWs are superstars at the community level! They use approved standing orders to treat common issues like malaria safely and quickly.

question: How do fat-soluble (lipid-soluble) toxins act differently in the body compared to water-soluble ones?

options.A: They cross cell membranes easily and can build up in fatty tissues
options.B: They immediately break down into harmless gas inside the stomach
options.C: They cannot enter the bloodstream unless injected directly into a vein
options.D: They are filtered out by the kidneys almost immediately upon entry

explanation: Because they love fat, these toxins slip easily through cell barriers and can stay stored in fatty tissues for a long time, prolonging their effects.

question: Which group of people should be involved during a community health situation analysis?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting local tourist attractions
options.B: International pharmaceutical company sales representatives
options.C: Local stakeholders like traditional leaders and women's groups
options.D: Only doctors from the federal capital city

explanation: True community health relies on involving local leaders and residents who understand their environment and hold social influence. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the main health benefit of encouraging child spacing through family planning after having a baby?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover its nutrient stores and strength.
options.B: It makes uterine involution happen within twenty-four hours.
options.C: It guarantees that the next baby will be a male child.
options.D: It completely stops all postpartum mood changes.

explanation: Pregnancy takes a lot out of a woman's body! Spacing pregnancies gives her time to rebuild her iron and nutrient levels so she stays strong for herself and her family.

question: Which chemical messenger relaxes blood vessels in the penis to start an erection?

options.A: Nitric oxide
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: When arousal happens, nerve endings release nitric oxide. This is the green light that relaxes the smooth muscles so blood can rush in.

question: Which drug class is commonly prescribed to cut down stomach acid and heal ulcers?

options.A: Osmotic laxatives
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Proton pump inhibitors
options.D: Anti-platelet agents

explanation: PPIs block the little 'pumps' in your stomach lining that make acid. Less acid means the ulcer finally gets a chance to heal up.

question: What size syringe should you use when trying to clear a blocked nasogastric tube?

options.A: 3 mL standard syringe
options.B: 1 mL insulin syringe
options.C: 5 mL tuberculin syringe
options.D: 30 mL or larger syringe

explanation: Always grab a 30 mL or bigger syringe! Small syringes build up too much pressure and can burst the plastic tubing, whereas bigger syringes spread out the force safely.

question: As a nurse, what is the best approach when checking thyroid lab results for a pregnant patient?

options.A: Ignoring the thyroid panel since hormones do not affect the gland
options.B: Immediately starting the patient on synthetic thyroid replacement
options.C: Using pregnancy-specific reference ranges instead of standard charts
options.D: Repeating the blood draw because the results are always inaccurate

explanation: Brilliant! Since a pregnant woman's baseline chemistry changes, you always want to use specialized pregnancy reference charts to read her labs correctly.

question: A hospital pharmacy prices an antibiotic by adding up the supplier price, shipping fees, storage power, and dispensing salaries. What costing approach is this?

options.A: Subsidized emergency pricing
options.B: Full operational cost recovery
options.C: Manufacturer retail pricing
options.D: Direct cost only approach

explanation: Spot on! Including both the price of the drug and all overhead expenses ensures the fund gets back every kobo spent to deliver care.

question: Which medication is absolutely essential for a patient living with Type 1 diabetes to survive?

options.A: Metformin
options.B: Acarbose
options.C: Sulfonylurea
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 bodies cannot make insulin, daily insulin replacement is a matter of survival. Another win for your clinical knowledge today!

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing style on two hospital wards without disrupting how the wards are already set up. What is the best study type?

options.A: Retrospective case-control study
options.B: Cross-sectional survey
options.C: Quasi-experimental study
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Correct! When you can't randomly mix up individual patients because of real-world ward setups, a quasi-experimental design saves the day. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a perk of using mucous membrane drug routes?

options.A: Bypassing harsh gastrointestinal fluids
options.B: Rapid entry into the bloodstream
options.C: Slowest possible onset of drug action
options.D: Usefulness for vomiting patients

explanation: Quite the opposite! Because mucous membranes are packed with blood vessels, they usually give a very fast onset of action, not a slow one.

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take when a patient shows signs of severe drug toxicity?

options.A: Stop the administration of the offending medication
options.B: Increase the intravenous fluid rate without a doctor's order
options.C: Document the event in the patient's chart at the end of the shift
options.D: Ask the patient to walk around the room to stay awake

explanation: Stopping the drug source prevents any more of the toxic substance from entering the patient's system. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why do many nurses feel more emotional weight when turning off a ventilator compared to deciding not to start one?

options.A: Because stopping an active machine feels like a direct action causing death
options.B: Because hospital policies strictly forbid withdrawing mechanical ventilation
options.C: Because family members are never allowed to witness ventilator removal
options.D: Because withholding treatment requires more paperwork than withdrawing

explanation: Physically reaching out to switch off life support feels heavy emotionally, even though ethically and legally, letting nature take its course is the same in both cases.

question: What is the number one nursing priority right after a patient has mouth or throat surgery?

options.A: Starting oral fluids within two hours
options.B: Maintaining a clear and open airway
options.C: Removing surgical dressings for inspection
options.D: Encouraging the patient to speak clearly

explanation: Swelling or bleeding after oral surgery can block breathing in a flash, making airway safety our top priority.

question: Which of these everyday activities is a classic example of NEAT (Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis)?

options.A: Running a scheduled marathon on Saturday morning
options.B: Lifting heavy weights at the gym for an hour
options.C: Pacing up and down the hospital hallway while on duty
options.D: Swimming laps in a competitive swimming pool

explanation: Exactly! As student nurses on clinical duty, all that walking, pacing, and running around the ward counts as NEAT—unplanned movement outside the gym!

question: Why do nurses and doctors pay very close attention when a lab report mentions dysplasia?

options.A: It guarantees that the tissue has already formed a malignant tumor
options.B: It causes immediate and total loss of function in the affected organ
options.C: It means the cells have permanently shrunk due to prolonged starvation
options.D: It represents disordered cellular growth that can progress to cancer

explanation: Dysplasia means the cells are looking disorganized and weird. Catching this early is key because it can sometimes turn into cancer if the stress doesn't stop.

question: What is a very common cause of false alarms on a portable pulse oximeter while moving a patient?

options.A: Normal room lighting brightness
options.B: Fresh battery installation
options.C: High room humidity levels
options.D: Motion artifact and shivering

explanation: Movement or shivering shakes the sensor around (motion artifact), confusing the machine and leading to wild or false readings.

question: What is a primary responsibility of community health nurses regarding food security?

options.A: Inspecting the mechanical engines of commercial cargo vehicles
options.B: Identifying nutritional deficits and educating vulnerable families
options.C: Setting international market prices for agricultural crops
options.D: Driving heavy trucks to transport harvests from farms to cities

explanation: Nurses assess nutritional health at the grassroots level and teach communities how to make the best use of available foods. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: What is the main job of the chairperson during a professional meeting?

options.A: Serving refreshments to all invited attendees
options.B: Guiding discussion and keeping the team on the agenda
options.C: Taking over patient care duties while staff are away
options.D: Writing down every single word spoken by participants

explanation: The chairperson leads the session, manages time, and ensures the group sticks to the planned topics.

question: Which waste product builds up in the blood to cause hepatic encephalopathy?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Ammonia
options.D: Sodium

explanation: A healthy liver turns nitrogen waste like ammonia into safe urea. When the liver fails, ammonia builds up and affects brain function, causing confusion.

question: What is the main goal of search and rescue operations when a disaster hits?

options.A: Clear debris and rebuild destroyed public infrastructure
options.B: Distribute food and clean water to affected communities
options.C: Locate, extricate, and deliver victims to medical care
options.D: Provide long-term rehabilitation for displaced families

explanation: You've got this! Search and rescue is simply about finding those who are missing, getting them out safely, and handing them over for medical treatment.

question: Why is the traditional mechanical approach to giving medications no longer enough?

options.A: It requires doctors to write more prescriptions
options.B: It prevents nurses from charting on computers
options.C: It ignores the patient's personal routine and individual needs
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy hospital shift

explanation: Simply handing over pills without considering the person's life often leads to poor adherence and missed doses. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is a common physical change that happens to the prostate gland as men age?

options.A: Total loss of the ability to produce seminal fluid
options.B: Complete shrinkage of the glandular tissue
options.C: Development of chronic bacterial infections in all men
options.D: Gradual enlargement that can affect urinary flow

explanation: You got it! The prostate tends to grow larger with age, which can sometimes press against the urethra and make urinating a bit tricky.

question: Which factor is most essential for MBO to succeed?

options.A: Strict orders from the chief medical director
options.B: Active participation from staff members
options.C: Frequent changes to nursing uniforms
options.D: Zero budget spending on training

explanation: Staff involvement is vital because people are more committed to goals they help design. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient with unsteady balance prepares for discharge home. What is the best nursing action to address home safety?

options.A: Discuss removing tripping hazards and installing bathroom grab bars
options.B: Advise the patient to remain in bed until fully recovered
options.C: Recommend replacing all furniture with hospital-grade equipment
options.D: Suggest wearing thick socks for warmth and comfort while walking

explanation: Practical modifications like clearing walkways and adding bathroom grab bars directly prevent falls in the living environment. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h7)

question: Why should you avoid writing vague words like 'normal' when charting a neurological exam?

options.A: It is illegal to use descriptive words in hospital charts
options.B: It prevents doctors from ordering blood laboratory tests
options.C: It automatically delays the patient's discharge process
options.D: It does not provide specific baseline data for future comparison

explanation: Spot on! Clear measurements and detailed descriptions help other nurses track exact changes over time.

question: What is the main difference between a normal and a maladaptive personality pattern?

options.A: Maladaptive patterns only appear in elderly patients with acute physical infections
options.B: Normal patterns never change, while maladaptive patterns disappear every few days
options.C: Maladaptive patterns are rigid and inflexible, causing distress and trouble with relationships
options.D: Normal patterns are entirely learned from television, while maladaptive ones are genetic

explanation: Maladaptive personality traits are rigid and cause ongoing personal distress and social friction, unlike flexible normal patterns. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT something a modern family planning nurse should do?

options.A: Reaching out to adolescents with friendly reproductive education
options.B: Promoting personalized contraceptive choices for patients
options.C: Forcing universal sterilization on rural communities
options.D: Expanding access to long-acting reversible contraceptives

explanation: Forced procedures go totally against human rights and good nursing. Care should always be voluntary and centered on what the patient wants!

question: Which of these is a great example of a drug working without using a receptor?

options.A: An insulin molecule attaching to a muscle cell
options.B: An opioid binding to a brain pain receptor
options.C: A beta-blocker slowing down the heart rate
options.D: An osmotic laxative pulling water into the bowel

explanation: Spot on! Osmotic laxatives rely on physical water movement rather than locking onto cellular receptors to do their job.

question: A patient comes in complaining of light spotting between her periods and after sex. Which condition is most likely?

options.A: Uterine fibroid
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.C: Ovarian cyst
options.D: Cervical polyp

explanation: Spotting between periods or right after intercourse is a classic giveaway for fragile cervical polyps!

question: Why do young women and girls often face a higher risk of new HIV infections in many communities?

options.A: Males do not contract the virus due to protective antibodies.
options.B: Biological differences and social inequalities intersect to increase their risk.
options.C: Healthcare workers screen boys less frequently than girls.
options.D: Females possess a genetic immunity that wears off during puberty.

explanation: Well done! Young women face both physical vulnerabilities and social factors like gender inequality that make it harder to negotiate safe sex.

question: A PAC patient is stable and ready to go home. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Provide compassionate contraceptive counseling and discharge instructions
options.B: Withhold discharge until a family elder arrives to sign papers
options.C: Scold the patient so she does not experience complications again
options.D: Prescribe heavy sedatives to prevent emotional processing

explanation: Before they leave, always give clear discharge notes and friendly, non-judgmental advice on how to prevent another unplanned pregnancy.

question: What are the two core behavioral areas used to understand autism?

options.A: Aggressive outbursts and profound sleepiness
options.B: Social communication challenges and repetitive behaviors
options.C: Hyperactivity and attention deficits
options.D: Memory loss and sudden physical paralysis

explanation: Spot on! Autism is primarily identified by differences in how a person communicates socially, alongside a preference for repetitive routines or movements.

question: Which of these is a classic example of primary disease prevention?

options.A: Screening adults for high blood pressure at a clinic
options.B: Treating a patient with active tuberculosis
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.D: Administering the polio vaccine to an infant

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention stops the disease from happening in the first place, and vaccination is the ultimate primary defense.

question: A teenage girl visits the clinic with recurrent chest infections and unusual linear burns across her breasts. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Breast ironing abuse
options.B: A severe allergic skin rash
options.C: Normal adolescent development
options.D: Accidental kitchen scalding

explanation: Unusual burn patterns and repeated infections on the chest during puberty are classic signs of breast ironing. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h6)

question: What do we mean by the term 'hidden hunger' in teenage nutrition?

options.A: Eating enough calories to feel full, but missing vital vitamins and minerals
options.B: An eating disorder where teenagers hide food
options.C: Feeling constantly starved despite eating three big meals
options.D: An inability to feel full after eating fiber

explanation: Brilliant! Hidden hunger happens when your belly feels full, but your body is still starving for the micronutrients it needs to thrive.

question: Which medication is commonly given during cardiac arrest to boost blood flow to the heart and brain?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Digoxin
options.D: Warfarin

explanation: You'll see epinephrine used often in codes! It acts as a powerful vasoconstrictor to push blood where it's needed most during resuscitation.

question: What happens in a vestibular hair cell when its hairs bend toward the tallest one (the kinocilium)?

options.A: The cell releases protective enzymes into the endolymph.
options.B: Calcium crystals dissolve into the surrounding perilymph.
options.C: Sodium channels close, leading to cell hyperpolarization.
options.D: Potassium channels open, leading to cell depolarization.

explanation: Bending toward the tallest hair stretches those tiny spring-like tip links, letting potassium in to excite the cell. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which of the following findings belongs in the review of systems?

options.A: A patient reporting occasional dizziness when standing up
options.B: A nurse measuring a blood pressure reading of 120/80 mmHg
options.C: A laboratory report showing a high white blood cell count
options.D: A surgeon finding an inflamed appendix during an operation

explanation: Dizziness reported by the patient is a subjective symptom, which is what the review of systems records. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: A hospital pharmacy is full of drugs, but the DRF has no cash because an insurance partner is six months late paying claims. What is this called?

options.A: A successful capitation profit
options.B: A cash flow bottleneck
options.C: An operational seed injection
options.D: A complete cost-recovery surplus

explanation: Spot on! When the money is trapped outside the hospital waiting on delayed payments, cash flow gets choked up, leaving you unable to place new orders.

question: What is the main goal of sling surgery done for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: To provide physical support under the urethra
options.B: To increase the total urine production rate
options.C: To shrink an enlarged prostate gland
options.D: To relax the overactive detrusor muscle

explanation: A sling creates a tiny hammock of mesh or tissue to lift and support the urethra so it stays shut when abdominal pressure spikes.

question: Where do most common front-of-the-nose nosebleeds start?

options.A: The olfactory bulb
options.B: Kiesselbach's plexus
options.C: The sphenoid wall
options.D: The ethmoid sinus

explanation: Correct! Kiesselbach's plexus is a busy network of tiny blood vessels right at the front partition of the nose, making it a very common spot for minor nosebleeds.

question: Why do nurses use numbers in the GCS instead of writing words like 'drowsy' in the patient's chart?

options.A: Doctors are not trained to read standard English descriptions
options.B: Words take too much time to write in a busy hospital chart
options.C: Numbers are the only way to bill insurance companies for care
options.D: Numerical scores prevent misunderstandings between different staff members

explanation: Words like 'drowsy' can mean different things to different nurses. A number gives everyone a clear, shared picture so we can easily track if the patient is getting better or worse.

question: What is one common drawback of giving medications through mucous membranes?

options.A: Guaranteed 100% absorption for every patient
options.B: Longer time to onset than oral tablets
options.C: Risk of local irritation and variable absorption
options.D: Elimination of the need for nurse verification

explanation: Tissues in the mouth, rectum, or eyes can sometimes get sore or irritated by potent drugs, and how fast they absorb can change depending on how moist or healthy the tissue is.

question: Which common lab test is used to screen patients for anemia?

options.A: Liver function enzymes
options.B: Serum lipid profile
options.C: Fast blood glucose
options.D: Hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: Checking hemoglobin and hematocrit tells us how well the blood carries oxygen, making it the go-to test for anemia.

question: What do we call a rehab goal that tries to stop side effects before they even happen?

options.A: Preventative goal
options.B: Supportive goal
options.C: Palliative goal
options.D: Restorative goal

explanation: Think of this as stopping trouble before it starts. Preventative rehab jumps in early to block expected physical losses.

question: Which of these statements about informed consent in qualitative interviews is FALSE?

options.A: It ensures participants know what the study is about
options.B: It protects the voluntary nature of participation
options.C: It only matters before the interview starts and is then forgotten
options.D: It is a continuous process that can be withdrawn at any time

explanation: You got it! Consent isn't just a paper signed at the beginning—a patient can change their mind and step out of the study at any point.

question: Which specific area in the frontal lobe is responsible for producing spoken language?

options.A: Wernicke's area
options.B: Broca's area
options.C: Prefrontal cortex
options.D: Motor strip

explanation: Broca's area handles the mechanical production of speech and language expression. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h2)

question: You just received a new delivery of canned milk for the clinic pantry. Where should you put the new cans?

options.A: On a separate table outside the storage room
options.B: In front of all the older cans for easy reach
options.C: In the refrigerator next to the fresh produce
options.D: Behind the older cans of milk already on the shelf

explanation: Always practice FIFO! Putting new stock behind older stock ensures the older items get used first before they spoil.

question: How do malignant cells often manage to survive even when a healthy immune system is present?

options.A: They absorb all circulating antibodies to block inflammation
options.B: They coat themselves in thick layers of calcium and iron
options.C: They turn into benign tumors to trick white blood cells
options.D: They release chemical signals that suppress immune cell activity

explanation: Well done! Clever cancer cells can send out decoy signals that turn down immune responses, tricking the body's defenses into leaving them alone.

question: Which insect transmits the parasite responsible for malaria?

options.A: Housefly
options.B: Tsetse fly
options.C: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.D: Blackfly

explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted specifically through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI?

options.A: To quickly screen for weight categories and health risks
options.B: To diagnose heart and metabolic diseases directly
options.C: To calculate exact daily food calories
options.D: To measure exact body fat percentage in muscles

explanation: BMI is a quick screening tool to help you spot weight categories that could lead to health issues. You're doing great!

question: Why does a patient with a severe bacterial infection often develop an elevated heart rate?

options.A: Body fluid shifts completely stop blood from reaching the heart
options.B: Fever and higher metabolic demand make the heart pump faster
options.C: Infections directly destroy the electrical pacemaker cells in the heart
options.D: White blood cells physically block the blood vessels and slow flow

explanation: Infections cause fever and raise the body's metabolic rate, which triggers the sympathetic nervous system to increase the heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h3)

question: When a patient resists your care during a home visit, what does it most likely mean?

options.A: Proof that the patient has fully recovered from illness
options.B: Fear and a desire to retain personal control and independence
options.C: A deliberate plot to get the nurse fired from the agency
options.D: A lack of respect for human rights laws in medicine

explanation: Correct! Resistance is often just a defense mechanism. Patients are usually scared of losing their independence and are trying to hold onto control of their lives.

question: Why is it important for the nurse to explain the rectal procedure thoroughly before beginning?

options.A: It guarantees that the drug will bypass liver metabolism
options.B: It replaces the need for wearing clean gloves during insertion
options.C: It helps reduce patient anxiety and embarrassment
options.D: It chemically speeds up the breakdown of the suppository base

explanation: The rectal procedure is sensitive and personal; clear communication builds trust and calms the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: What does the detrusor muscle do while your body is storing urine normally?

options.A: It undergoes rapid skeletal muscle spasms.
options.B: It relaxes to accommodate accumulating urine.
options.C: It completely stops receiving all blood supply.
options.D: It contracts forcefully to expel bladder contents.

explanation: To hold urine comfortably without building up too much pressure, the detrusor muscle needs to relax and stretch out. You're crushing this topic!

question: What does it mean to write a 'contemporaneous' nursing note?

options.A: It is written using official medical shorthand
options.B: It is written at the end of the entire work week
options.C: It is written close to the time care is given
options.D: It is written by a senior doctor only

explanation: Spot on! Writing notes right away means you don't have to rely on memory, keeping the true timeline safe.

question: Why are bariatric (weight-loss) surgery patients told not to drink fluids at the same time they eat solid meals?

options.A: To prevent the stomach from overfilling and to avoid triggering dumping syndrome
options.B: To prevent the absorption of any vitamins or minerals
options.C: To make digestion take as long as humanly possible
options.D: To ensure they lose as much water weight as possible

explanation: Correct! Drinking water with meals washes the food through a tiny stomach pouch too quickly, causing discomfort and cramping.

question: Which of the following is a well-known long-term reproductive complication of untreated salpingitis?

options.A: Hypertrophy of the external genitalia
options.B: Tubal factor infertility
options.C: Development of uterine fibroid tumors
options.D: Permanent cessation of all menses

explanation: Tubal scarring can block the path entirely, making it very difficult for sperm and egg to meet, which can lead to fertility challenges.

question: What is the main reason we group and organize medical supplies in a ward?

options.A: To reduce the total number of items ordered each month
options.B: To prevent medication errors and speed up retrieval
options.C: To make the pharmacy department look neat and tidy
options.D: To ensure patients pay higher fees for their treatments

explanation: A well-organized ward helps you find what you need in a hurry. When every second counts, clear placement keeps your patients safe and cuts down on mistakes.

question: A head nurse times how long it takes staff to complete morning vitals to eliminate wasted steps. Which management approach is being used?

options.A: Contingency approach
options.B: Systems theory
options.C: Scientific management
options.D: Human relations theory

explanation: Using time studies and analyzing physical movements to optimize workflow is the core of scientific management. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is vitamin D production in the skin important for bone health?

options.A: It increases red blood cell production in marrow
options.B: It lubricates the joints to prevent stiffness
options.C: It helps the digestive tract absorb calcium properly
options.D: It keeps the skin surface strong and waterproof

explanation: Active vitamin D is essential for the intestines to absorb dietary calcium, which keeps bones strong. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h5)

question: If a patient gets infected through a mosquito bite, what type of transmission is this?

options.A: Feco-oral route
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Congenital transmission

explanation: Easy peasy! A 'vector' is like a living taxi (like a mosquito) that carries the parasite from one person to another.

question: What causes a high ventilation-perfusion mismatch, like when someone has a pulmonary embolism?

options.A: Air reaches the alveoli, but blood flow is blocked
options.B: Deoxygenated blood bypasses the lungs entirely through a shunt
options.C: Blood flows normally, but the airways are completely filled with pus
options.D: Surface tension drops so low that the alveoli permanently swell

explanation: Well done! A pulmonary embolism blocks blood flow past the air sacs, meaning air gets in fine, but there's no blood there to pick it up. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h3)

question: What does the term 'countertransference' mean in nursing?

options.A: When the hospital administration changes a patient's care assignment
options.B: When the nurse projects personal feelings or unresolved issues onto the patient
options.C: When the patient projects feelings from past relationships onto the nurse
options.D: When communication breaks down due to language and cultural barriers

explanation: Countertransference happens when you accidentally let your own personal emotions, memories, or biases spill over onto how you treat a patient.

question: According to the World Health Organization, what BMI value marks the start of the overweight category?
explanation: The overweight category officially starts at a BMI of 25.0 and goes up to 29.9. You are learning fast!

question: Why should a nurse avoid using household kitchen spoons to measure liquid medications?

options.A: Using them makes the liquid spill on the table
options.B: Household spoons react chemically with liquid drugs
options.C: Kitchen spoons are too heavy for patients to hold
options.D: Kitchen spoons vary in size and give inaccurate doses

explanation: Household spoons are not standardized for medical measurements, which can lead to giving too much or too little medicine. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which of the following is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor?

options.A: Biological sex at birth
options.B: Family history of heart disease
options.C: Elevated blood pressure
options.D: Advanced chronological age

explanation: Blood pressure can be modified through diet, exercise, and medication, whereas age, sex, and genetics cannot be changed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why do you need to be very careful when doing joint exercises for an elderly client with severe osteoporosis?

options.A: Their blood circulation is already too fast
options.B: Their skin is prone to rashes easily
options.C: Their muscles will become too bulky too quickly
options.D: Their fragile bones are at high risk of breaking

explanation: Exactly! Osteoporosis makes bones weak and brittle, so gentle handling is key to preventing accidental fractures.

question: In research, what does the 'validity' of a questionnaire mean?

options.A: Whether the tool can be completed in under ten minutes
options.B: Whether the tool measures what it is intended to measure
options.C: Whether the tool was printed on approved institutional paper
options.D: Whether the tool gives the exact same scores on repeat testing

explanation: Validity checks if your questions are truly capturing the specific concept or variable you set out to study. You're building solid clinical research skills!

question: What is the main job of 'tail coverage' when using a claims-made insurance policy?

options.A: To lower the monthly premium cost for brand new graduate nurses
options.B: To cover claims filed after the policy has expired for incidents that happened during the active period
options.C: To pay for accidental property damage inside the hospital breakroom
options.D: To provide extra financial compensation if the nurse is injured on duty

explanation: Tail coverage acts like a safety bridge when you leave a job or retire, protecting you from late lawsuits about past shifts.

question: What sudden change is a classic early warning sign that a home care patient's heart failure is getting worse?

options.A: An increased appetite for high-fiber green vegetables
options.B: A sudden weight gain of two pounds or more overnight
options.C: A gradual increase in daily physical exercise tolerance
options.D: An unexpected drop in resting daytime heart rate

explanation: Spot on! When the heart isn't pumping efficiently, fluid builds up fast. An overnight weight jump is one of the earliest red flags for worsening heart failure.

question: In disaster triage systems like START, what does the color RED mean?

options.A: Minor cuts and sprains for walking wounded patients
options.B: Stable injuries that can safely wait several hours
options.C: Deceased victims or injuries with zero chance of survival
options.D: Immediate life-threatening injuries needing rapid care

explanation: You nailed it! Red means red alert—these patients need instant medical attention to save their lives.

question: A patient at 32 weeks reports she has not felt her baby move all day. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Mild physiological anemia of pregnancy
options.B: Potential fetal distress or compromise
options.C: Standard weight gain in the third trimester
options.D: Normal resting behavior of a mature fetus

explanation: Whenever a mom says baby's movements have stopped or slowed right down, treat it as an emergency and check the baby right away.

question: A patient is admitted to the ward with severe dehydration and a dry, cracked tongue. What primary mechanical function of the tongue is most likely impaired?

options.A: Directly absorbing simple sugars directly through the taste buds
options.B: Moving and shaping food into a smooth bolus for swallowing
options.C: Filtering dust particles away from the lower respiratory airway
options.D: Producing the primary digestive enzymes needed for starch breakdown

explanation: Dehydration affects oral tissues, making it hard for the tongue to move and moisten food properly into a smooth bolus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h3)

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.B: Staff, Bedside, Admission, Review
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.D: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Result

explanation: You got it! SBAR is your best friend when calling a doctor or handing over a patient. It keeps your message clear, short, and professional.

question: What is the primary focus of a hospice home facility?

options.A: Delivering intensive acute surgical care
options.B: Testing experimental medical treatments
options.C: Providing comfort and quality of life
options.D: Achieving a full recovery from terminal illness

explanation: Hospice care shifts away from curative treatments and focuses entirely on keeping the patient comfortable and improving their quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h1)

question: What important tip should you give a patient taking a delayed-release PPI capsule?

options.A: Swallow the capsule whole without chewing or crushing it
options.B: Chew the capsule thoroughly before swallowing with water
options.C: Dissolve the capsule completely in warm lemon juice first
options.D: Open the capsule and mix the powder directly into milk

explanation: Those capsules have a special coating to protect the medicine from stomach acid until it gets where it needs to be. Chewing ruins that protection!

question: Which drug tragedy in the 1950s and 1960s caused severe birth defects and completely changed global drug safety rules?

options.A: Sulfanilamide
options.B: Thalidomide
options.C: Penicillin
options.D: Paracetamol

explanation: Spot on! Thalidomide was prescribed for morning sickness back then, but it sadly caused severe limb defects in babies, forcing the world to tighten up drug safety laws.

question: What does a positively skewed distribution tell us about patient recovery times?

options.A: The data contains an equal number of fast and slow recoveries
options.B: Most patients take a long time to recover, with very few fast recoveries
options.C: All patients recover in the exact same number of days
options.D: Most patients recover quickly, but a few take a very long time

explanation: Spot on! A positive skew means most people recover fast (piled up at the start), but a few stubborn cases drag the tail out toward longer recovery times.

question: What is the main limitation of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) compared to an EHR?

options.A: It is usually restricted to a single facility or clinic
options.B: It cannot be viewed by registered nurses or doctors
options.C: It only contains billing information and insurance forms
options.D: It is always written on paper rather than typed digitally

explanation: Good job! An EMR is great for one specific clinic's digital files, but it doesn't easily share that info with outside hospitals.

question: What must you check before giving a patient water after an upper GI scope?

options.A: That the patient's gag reflex has fully returned
options.B: That the patient's blood pressure is above normal
options.C: That the doctor has reviewed all laboratory results
options.D: That the patient has passed normal flatus

explanation: Their throat is usually numbed during the test. Checking for the gag reflex ensures they won't choke when they finally take a sip of water!

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that means a home birth must be stopped and transferred immediately?

options.A: Craving unusual foods
options.B: Swelling of the fingers in hot weather
options.C: Mild tiredness after walking
options.D: Heavy vaginal bleeding during labor

explanation: Heavy bleeding is a sign of a dangerous obstetric emergency like placental abruption or previa, needing urgent hospital care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h7)

question: High rates of under-five mortality in a community usually point to problems with which of the following?

options.A: Preventable infections and nutrition
options.B: Lack of secondary school education for adults
options.C: High rates of retirement among elderly workers
options.D: Excessive spending on surgical equipment

explanation: Child deaths under five are largely driven by malnutrition, poor sanitation, and preventable childhood infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the main job of agar in microbiology culture media?

options.A: To solidify liquid broth into a solid growth surface
options.B: To lower the temperature inside laboratory incubators
options.C: To provide extra oxygen for anaerobic bacteria
options.D: To stain bacterial cells under a light microscope

explanation: You nailed it! Agar comes from seaweed and acts like gelatin, turning liquid broth into a firm plate where colonies can grow nicely.

question: Why must you mention pending lab tests or investigations during a shift report?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that tests are expensive
options.B: So the patient can decide whether to cancel the appointment
options.C: So the incoming nurse can monitor preparation and follow up on results
options.D: To ensure the laboratory staff receive extra break time

explanation: Tests often need special preparation before and tracking after, which becomes the job of the incoming shift.

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a person feel before taking health action?

options.A: Vulnerable to the disease and aware of its seriousness
options.B: Fully trained to treat others with the same condition
options.C: Required by local law to report to a health facility
options.D: Financially compensated for visiting the local clinic

explanation: People only change their health habits when they realize, 'This sickness can actually affect me, and it is quite serious!' That's the heart of the Health Belief Model. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h3)

question: A child spends all day selling pure water in traffic but goes home to sleep with their parents every night. How do we classify this child?

options.A: A child on the street
options.B: An abandoned minor
options.C: A child of the street
options.D: A completely emancipated ward

explanation: Great job! Kids 'on the street' work or spend their days outdoors, but they still have a home base to return to every night.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier when nursing vulnerable families?

options.A: Extreme poverty pushing health down the priority list
options.B: Cultural beliefs about what causes sickness
options.C: Having too much financial wealth and multiple luxury cars
options.D: Not having money for clinic transport

explanation: Spot on! Wealth is the opposite of vulnerability. Real barriers include poverty, transport costs, and conflicting cultural views.

question: Which international organization has the main global job of protecting and helping refugees?

options.A: UNESCO
options.B: FIFA
options.C: OPEC
options.D: UNHCR

explanation: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) leads the charge globally in safeguarding refugees and finding long-term solutions for displaced people.

question: A Nigerian nurse is talking with a mother during a routine immunization visit. What is a great way to use this time for nutrition?

options.A: Share practical tips on using affordable local foods for good health
options.B: Focus strictly on vaccine schedules and ignore dietary questions
options.C: Delay nutrition talk until the child develops a severe deficiency
options.D: Advise the mother to buy expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: You nailed it! Routine clinic visits are the ideal moment to chat with mothers and encourage them to use affordable, local foods to keep their little ones strong.

question: Which life stage has the fastest human growth rate, coming in second right after infancy?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Toddlerhood
options.C: Young adulthood
options.D: Middle childhood

explanation: You've got this! Adolescence is well known as the second fastest period of human growth, right behind infancy. Your body is doing amazing things during these teenage years!

question: Why might a doctor order a CA-125 blood test for a patient with an ovarian mass?

options.A: To diagnose a sudden bacterial infection in the pelvis
options.B: To check if the patient is currently pregnant
options.C: To help check for markers associated with ovarian cancer
options.D: To measure the exact amount of estrogen in the blood

explanation: CA-125 is just a protein marker in the blood that can go up when certain ovarian growths are present. It helps doctors get a clearer picture!

question: What tool do midwives use during labor to track contractions, dilation, and baby's heart rate on one sheet?

options.A: Temperature chart
options.B: Immunization card
options.C: Partograph
options.D: Admission register

explanation: You got it! The partograph is a nurse's best friend in the labor room for spotting trouble early and keeping track of progress.

question: Which type of artificial fat, made by industrial processing, is best avoided entirely?

options.A: Monounsaturated fats
options.B: Naturally occurring saturated fats
options.C: Polyunsaturated fats
options.D: Trans fats

explanation: Trans fats are man-made to make processed foods last longer on shelves, but they are very hard on our hearts and best avoided.

question: Which activity is a great example of promoting worker health on the job?

options.A: Auditing company financial accounts and tax returns
options.B: Purchasing new raw materials for factory production
options.C: Negotiating labor union salary contracts
options.D: Organizing lifestyle wellness campaigns and health screenings

explanation: Spot on! Health promotion is all about proactive care—like checking blood pressure or teaching healthy habits right there at the workplace.

question: Which action represents the correct use of alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Applying the rub and wiping the hands dry quickly with a cloth towel
options.B: Applying the rub and rubbing hands together until the solution is completely dry
options.C: Rinsing the hands with clean water right after applying the rub
options.D: Applying the rub only when wearing sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Alcohol rubs need to air-dry completely on the skin to achieve their full germ-killing effect. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main focus of efficiency in a healthcare plan?

options.A: Getting maximum results with minimum waste of resources
options.B: Spending the entire annual budget before the year ends
options.C: Employing as many administrative workers as possible
options.D: Purchasing the most expensive medical equipment available

explanation: Efficiency is all about making the best use of limited supplies, money, and staff time without unnecessary waste.

question: Why do nurses need to check complete blood counts (CBC) regularly for patients on carbamazepine?

options.A: To check how well the kidneys are filtering excess water
options.B: To confirm that the patient is eating enough iron-rich foods
options.C: To monitor for bone marrow suppression and low blood cell counts
options.D: To measure the exact amount of calcium stored in the bones

explanation: Carbamazepine can sometimes slow down the bone marrow's ability to make blood cells. Regular blood tests help us catch any dangerous drops in red or white blood cells early.

question: In community health statistics, what does 'incidence' tell us?

options.A: The total number of all old and new cases in a population
options.B: The percentage of infected patients who die from the disease
options.C: The number of new cases of a disease over a specific time
options.D: The expected baseline level of an illness in a community

explanation: Think of incidence as new arrivals! It counts brand-new cases popping up so nurses can see how fast an illness is currently spreading.

question: Why might a patient having a severe gout flare still show a completely normal blood uric acid level on a lab test?

options.A: Blood tests are completely useless for diagnosing joint pain
options.B: Uric acid only travels through the urine, not the bloodstream
options.C: Blood tests cannot detect uric acid when a person is in pain
options.D: Uric acid can temporarily drop during an acute inflammation flare

explanation: Brilliant! During an actual flare, uric acid levels in the blood can dip down to normal ranges, meaning a blood test alone can sometimes play tricks on you.

question: What physical sign on a skin boil strongly points to a live, breathing larva hidden underneath?

options.A: Bright yellow pus dripping freely
options.B: A small central pore or opening
options.C: A completely smooth, shiny surface
options.D: A large black crust or scab

explanation: Buried larvae need to breathe just like we do! They keep a tiny central hole open at the skin surface so they can get air.

question: Besides hands-on technical procedures, what major professional skill is greatly improved through simulation teamwork?

options.A: Effective communication and team coordination
options.B: Advanced medical billing and coding
options.C: Hospital accounting and financial budgeting
options.D: Maintenance of hospital medical equipment

explanation: Simulation scenarios require students to talk clearly, assign roles, and work together as a cohesive healthcare unit. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the most important screening test nurses should encourage to catch early cell changes on the cervix?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Pap smear
options.C: CA-125 blood test
options.D: Endometrial biopsy
