options.C: Fats
options.D: Water

explanation: Carbohydrates break down rapidly into glucose during digestion, causing a direct rise in blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h2)

question: Which common infrastructure problem makes it hard to store medications like insulin in patient homes?

options.A: Unreliable electricity grids
options.B: Frequent fuel price increases
options.C: Poor telecommunication networks
options.D: Inadequate road construction

explanation: Well done! Drugs that need a fridge, like insulin, struggle when power supply is erratic.

question: How do bile salts help your body digest fats?

options.A: Breaking large fat globules into tiny emulsified droplets
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes directly into the fat droplets
options.C: Neutralizing stomach acid before fats reach the intestine
options.D: Chemically dissolving fats into simple fatty acids

explanation: Bile salts act just like dish soap, turning big globs of fat into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily reach them.

question: Which of these is NOT something a home care nurse tracks when evaluating a client's progress?

options.A: Tracking how many television channels the client watches daily
options.B: Monitoring whether vital signs like blood pressure are stabilizing
options.C: Assessing whether surgical or chronic wounds are healing properly
options.D: Observing if functional abilities like walking are improving

explanation: Spot on! We focus on health stats, wound healing, and daily strength—not how much TV they watch!

question: Why did Nigeria adopt the Expanded Programme on Immunization framework?

options.A: To replace traditional herbal medicine practitioners entirely
options.B: To generate revenue for local government health clinics
options.C: To combat high rates of preventable childhood mortality
options.D: To manage emergency trauma cases from road traffic accidents

explanation: The initiative was localized to address and lower the heavy burden of death caused by infectious childhood diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: How do private health insurance companies usually decide how much you will pay for your monthly premium?

options.A: Based on the current weather and seasonal changes
options.B: Based on the patient's favorite recreational activities
options.C: Based on the total population size of the country
options.D: Based on age, medical history, and lifestyle risks

explanation: That's right! Private insurers look at your health history and risks to set prices, meaning older individuals or those with ongoing conditions often pay a bit more.

question: A nursing student writes this objective: 'To study everything about nurses.' Which SMART rule does this break the most?

options.A: Specific
options.B: Financial
options.C: Time-bound
options.D: Ethical

explanation: Saying 'everything about nurses' is way too broad! A good objective needs to be Specific so you know exactly what corner of nursing you are investigating. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h5)

question: A patient says, 'I cannot be healthy because I am too weak to go to work and look after my children.' Which health model are they using?

options.A: Clinical model
options.B: Role performance model
options.C: Eudaimonistic model
options.D: Biological germ model

explanation: Spot on! This model measures health by whether a person can successfully carry out their daily family and job responsibilities.

question: What is the very first step in the community mobilisation process?

options.A: Building a permanent hospital
options.B: Evaluating project funds
options.C: Mass immunisation
options.D: Entry and sensitization

explanation: Before doing anything else, health workers must properly introduce themselves and gain entry through appropriate community channels. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is formal accreditation important for a home health care agency?

options.A: It guarantees the agency will never face financial losses
options.B: It replaces the need for any clinical documentation
options.C: It allows nurses to prescribe medications without a doctor
options.D: It proves the agency meets established safety and operational benchmarks

explanation: Think of accreditation as a trusted stamp of approval. It proves through independent review that the agency operates safely and follows recognized standards.

question: Why is clear communication so vital during home health visits?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical assessments entirely
options.B: It helps build trust and gathers accurate health data
options.C: It guarantees the patient will recover within a week
options.D: It prevents the family from asking questions

explanation: Spot on! Since you are working independently out in the field, talking openly is your best tool to truly understand what's happening in the patient's daily life.

question: If a baby's head enters the pelvis leading with the longest chin-to-forehead (mentoventricular) measurement, what is the likely outcome?

options.A: Labour will proceed rapidly because this is the smallest skull measurement.
options.B: The baby is in an ideal position for a normal spontaneous delivery.
options.C: The head will easily mould to fit through the pelvic outlet without issues.
options.D: Vaginal birth is extremely difficult or impossible due to the large size.

explanation: At 14 centimeters, this is the biggest measurement of the head. It's too wide to easily fit through, which usually makes a normal vaginal delivery very difficult.

question: What common emotional challenge do family caregivers often face when a patient returns home on leave?

options.A: High levels of anxiety and fear regarding potential relapse
options.B: Excessive anger because the hospital cures patients too quickly
options.C: Confusion caused by sudden physical weight gain
options.D: Complete boredom due to the patient's lack of needs

explanation: It's completely normal for families to feel anxious and worry about handling unexpected symptom flare-ups at home.

question: A patient having an emergency heart attack goes to the nearest hospital without comparing prices. Why does this situation break normal market rules?

options.A: Urgent medical needs eliminate the ability to shop around
options.B: Hospitals are legally required to match competitor rates
options.C: Governments strictly ban price tags in emergency rooms
options.D: Emergency care is always free of charge

explanation: True market dynamics require consumers to compare options, which is impossible during life-threatening medical emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h2)

question: What do we call the infected clumps of platelets and germs that grow on heart valves in endocarditis?

options.A: Atheromas
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Thromboemboli

explanation: In infective endocarditis, clusters of bacteria, platelets, and fibrin build up on the valves like little growths called vegetations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: What does a Non-Stress Test (NST) actually check for?

options.A: Fetal heart rate changes in response to movement
options.B: The maturity of the fetal lungs before delivery
options.C: The exact amount of protein in maternal urine
options.D: Maternal blood pressure fluctuations over time

explanation: An NST looks at how the baby's heart rate reacts when they move around. A healthy baby's heart rate speeds up a bit with movement—simple and non-invasive!

question: What do we call it when cancer cells break away and spread to other parts of the body through the blood or lymph system?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Mitosis
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Hyperplasia

explanation: You've got this! Metastasis is simply the word for when cancer travels from its original spot to start new tumors elsewhere. Great job!

question: When do we typically expect a secondary postpartum haemorrhage to happen?

options.A: During the immediate pushing of the placenta
options.B: Only after the baby stops breastfeeding completely
options.C: Within the first two hours after a CS
options.D: Between 24 hours and six weeks after delivery

explanation: Secondary PPH shows up later—anytime from 24 hours up to six weeks postpartum. It's usually caused by tiny bits of leftover tissue or an infection.

question: What is the 'red reflex' during an ophthalmoscopic exam?

options.A: A warning light on the handle indicating low battery power
options.B: An abnormal sign of bleeding inside the front of the eye
options.C: A reddish-orange glow reflecting off the patient's retina
options.D: The natural color of the iris when exposed to bright light

explanation: The red reflex is the normal reddish-orange reflection of light seen through the pupil, confirming that the optical pathway is clear. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for terminal patients at home?

options.A: Finding a surgical cure for advanced cancer
options.B: Testing new experimental drugs that reverse aging
options.C: Isolating the patient from all family and friends
options.D: Providing comfort, symptom control, and preserving dignity

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and managing symptoms to ensure the highest possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which urethral sphincter can you consciously control using your skeletal muscles?

options.A: Internal urethral sphincter
options.B: Bladder neck sphincter
options.C: Prostatic urethral sphincter
options.D: External urethral sphincter

explanation: Awesome! The external sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, which gives you voluntary control over when you pee.

question: What term describes two different observers getting similar results when watching the same event?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: Participant bias
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Structured validity

explanation: Well done! 'Inter-rater reliability' simply means different observers agree and are consistent in how they score what they see.

question: How does community participation influence the success of a primary health care program?

options.A: It ensures the community accepts and sustains the health interventions
options.B: It guarantees that every resident becomes a trained community health worker
options.C: It removes the need for government funding of local health posts
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all administrative duties to villagers

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and support them long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h2)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triad used to study diseases?

options.A: Infection, illness, and recovery
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Vector, parasite, and human
options.D: Bacteria, virus, and protozoa

explanation: Spot on! The epidemiological triad looks at the interacting relationship between the agent, the host, and their environment to understand how diseases spread.

question: Why is it important to formally retire older, outdated protocols when introducing a new one?

options.A: It clears away mental and physical space so new practices can take root
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not have to write any more prescriptions
options.C: It prevents patients from reading old medical textbooks in the library
options.D: It saves money on printing paper for the hospital administration office

explanation: Stopping old, useless habits prevents confusion and reduces the workload burden on busy nurses. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which common germ is famous for resisting standard drugs like methicillin?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.C: Streptococcus mutans
options.D: Clostridium tetani

explanation: You'll hear a lot about MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) in clinicals—it's a classic example of a tough, drug-resistant bug.

question: What organ acts as the lungs and kidneys for a developing fetus?

options.A: The liver
options.B: The placenta
options.C: The fetal kidneys
options.D: The amniotic sac

explanation: Before birth, the placenta handles oxygen exchange and waste removal since the fetal lungs and kidneys are not yet functional. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: What should a nurse do if a patient consistently eats less than 30 percent of their food?

options.A: Wait two weeks to see if appetite returns on its own
options.B: Notify the dietitian and consider nutritional support options
options.C: Tell the patient that eating is mandatory for discharge
options.D: Remove all meal trays immediately without documenting intake

explanation: Poor intake puts patients at risk for malnutrition. Always team up with the dietitian early to help your patient get the nutrition they need!

question: What is a major benefit of buying local Nigerian food staples during harvest season?

options.A: They are always imported from abroad
options.B: They have longer artificial shelf lives
options.C: They require no washing or cooking
options.D: They are cheaper and more nutritious

explanation: In-season local foods are harvested at peak ripeness, offering better nutrients at lower market prices due to high supply. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h7)

question: Which communication technique helps encourage a patient to open up about their feelings?

options.A: Offering false reassurance
options.B: Changing the conversation topic
options.C: Giving immediate advice
options.D: Asking open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions (like 'How have you been sleeping lately?') invite patients to share their story freely instead of just nodding with a simple yes or no.

question: What major public health threat is directly worsened by the over-prescription of antibiotics?

options.A: High blood pressure rates
options.B: Chronic kidney stone disease
options.C: Antimicrobial resistance
options.D: Nutritional vitamin deficiencies

explanation: Unnecessary antibiotic use teaches bacteria how to survive drug treatments, creating resistant strains that are hard to cure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: What common facial feature is often seen during the active dying phase because muscles completely relax?

options.A: Flushed cheeks
options.B: A sagging jaw
options.C: Widened eyes
options.D: A tight grimace

explanation: When facial muscles lose all their tone, the jaw naturally sags open during the active dying phase. Every clinical detail you learn makes you a better nurse!

question: If a nursing mother's diet lacks enough nutrients, how does her body manage to produce breast milk?

options.A: The body absorbs extra nutrients directly from the air
options.B: Milk production stops completely until diet improves
options.C: The body draws from maternal stores to maintain milk
options.D: Breast milk loses all its essential nutrients instantly

explanation: Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs! If diet falls short, the mother's body will use its own stored nutrients to keep the milk flowing. Great job understanding maternal priority!

question: Why do normal lab test values change when a woman is pregnant?

options.A: Pregnant women have a slower metabolic rate overall
options.B: Blood cells shrink in size during the first trimester
options.C: The laboratory equipment is calibrated differently for women
options.D: Pregnancy hormones significantly alter baseline body chemistry

explanation: Think of pregnancy as a total body makeover! Because hormones shift so much, the normal lab ranges you use for non-pregnant patients simply don't apply here.

question: What is a major goal of health education when a community is facing an epidemic?

options.A: Encouraging early health-seeking behavior
options.B: Discouraging people from visiting hospitals
options.C: Increasing community fear of the disease
options.D: Promoting traditional medical practices

explanation: Spot on! Good health education encourages people to report symptoms early so treatment can start before complications set in.

question: A community nurse notices that an elderly client's primary caregiver looks extremely exhausted and frustrated. What is the best way to document this observation?

options.A: Record specific behavioral signs of fatigue in the caregiver and note the risk of burnout
options.B: Write that the family member is lazy and refuses to help the sick client
options.C: Document that the home environment is completely peaceful and supportive
options.D: Ignore the observation because the family member is not the official client

explanation: Documenting caregiver strain objectively helps the healthcare team plan interventions to support the family and protect the client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: When can a patient typically start a new method of birth control after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting for three full menstrual cycles
options.B: Before taking the initial dose of mifepristone
options.C: Six months after the procedure is completed
options.D: Immediately or at the follow-up visit

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Most birth control methods can be started right away on the day the abortion process is complete.

question: Why is it important to tailor teaching to a patient's literacy and language level?

options.A: It speeds up the nursing documentation process at the end of the shift
options.B: Federal laws prohibit speaking medical terminology in private homes
options.C: It ensures the patient can truly understand and follow self-care steps
options.D: Patients with low literacy cannot operate any form of medical equipment

explanation: Education only works if the patient understands it; matching their language and literacy ensures they can manage their condition safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h5)

question: How often should a bedbound patient usually be turned to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Every thirty minutes
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes pressure off bony areas and protects their skin from breaking down. Great routine to master for clinicals!

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain.

question: Why are cooking demonstrations more effective than simply handing out printed pamphlets?

options.A: They show mothers how to use local foods in practical, hands-on ways
options.B: They eliminate the need for any further nursing follow-up
options.C: They prove that imported foods are always superior
options.D: They take less time than talking to individuals

explanation: Hands-on cooking demos help learners visualize and practice preparing nutritious meals with ingredients they already own. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)
